summary: PLAN_REVIEW complete, iteration 0. Outcome not_converged: 10 distinct blocking findings across four independent reviewers (claude_code/opus-5 primary + antigravity/gemini-3.6-flash-medium + codex/gpt-5.5 + grok-4.5; pi failed with the known Invalid-JSON-output mode, quorum 3/4 vendors + primary). 41 raw findings merged. IMPORTANT: consensus-plan.json reports blocking_count=0 — that is a lexical-matching artifact of consensus_synthesizer.py (it marks a finding confirmed only when descriptions match above a similarity threshold; four reviewers described the same defects in different words), NOT an absence of blocking findings. Cross-confirmation was done manually and is recorded below. The two carried-forward review targets both resolved: (1) D13's CORE mechanism survives review — three reviewers independently judged the forward-per-document / reverse-per-capability split sound and the D12-redundancy distinction real, and grok verified by grep that no residual single-switch text survives; every blocking finding against D13 is at its EDGES (malformed switch artifact, cross-capability exclusions, zero-contracts capability, opt-in transition under change scope). (2) The PLAN_ITERATE refutation of the gatekeeper's wp-model write_allow widening is CORRECT — independently verified by all four reviewers against the real models and generators, with no dissent; the gatekeeper's suggestion must not be re-applied. Separately, a DIFFERENT invalidated-file instance that neither prior phase found IS real: task 2.0's schema promotion invalidates docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md, which no package may write.
completed_work: Read all plan artifacts in the managed worktree on branch openspec/trace-requirements-to-contracts: proposal.md, design.md (D1-D13), specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md (14 ADDED requirements / 35 scenarios), specs/skill-workflow/spec.md (1 MODIFIED + 1 ADDED), tasks.md (5 phases, 44 tasks), work-packages.yaml (5 packages + 6 [human] carve-outs), both contract schemas and contracts/README.md, plus the GATEKEEPER and PLAN_ITERATE PhaseRecords.

Produced 20 primary findings at review-findings-plan.json, schema-validated against openspec/schemas/review-findings.schema.json (severity spread: 7 critical / 7 nit / 1 optional / 1 fyi / 4 none; axes: correctness 11, architecture 8, readability 1).

Dispatched multi-vendor review via review_dispatcher.py --mode review with a prompt that named D13 and the wp-model dispute as priority targets and instructed empirical verification. All non-claude vendors run review mode with command execution available (codex `exec -s read-only`, grok `--always-approve`, agy `--mode plan` with headless permission grant), so reviewers executed checks rather than only reading.
Vendor results: antigravity 5 findings (81s), codex 5 findings (315s), grok 11 findings (312s), pi failed 'Invalid JSON output' at 1.6s. Manifest at reviews/review-manifest.json.
Ran consensus_synthesizer.py over all four sets -> reviews/consensus-plan.json (41 findings, quorum met 4/4).

Independently verified empirical claims rather than trusting prose. D2's slug algorithm reimplemented over all 29 openspec/specs/*/spec.md: 632 requirement headings, 0 identifiers failing traceability.schema.json's citation pattern, 0 intra-capability collisions — matches the design exactly.

Verified the wp-model dispute at the source: interface-descriptor.schema.json $defs = {AuthConfig, BudgetConfig, CommandSpec, EndpointSpec, FileInterfaceMapping, McpToolSpec, ServiceSpec, StartupConfig, StateVerifier}; FlagSpec/PositionalSpec/ToolCommandSpec/OperationSpec absent because ToolDescriptor/ServiceDescriptor are subclasses and generate_contract_schemas.py renders InterfaceDescriptor only. generate_tool_descriptor.py dumps flags/positionals/commands with exclude_defaults=True (lines 121/129/136).

Verified the api.contracts producer's inventory coupling: producer_api_contracts.py rglobs openspec/contracts/**/*.schema.json into docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md, which carries a schema COUNT (currently '_13 contract schema(s)._') and one row per schema; the context-drift-gate CI job fails on drift. Ran the gate on the current tree: outcome 'fresh', exit 0 — so the drift would be newly introduced by task 2.0.

Verified the capability-naming divergence: openspec/contracts/ holds phase-record, project-context-refresh and prototyping, none of which has an openspec/specs/<name>/spec.md (the spec tree has project-context-refresh-orchestration and -records instead). openspec/contracts/README.md documents capability as a short label, not a spec dir name.

Verified skills/tests/validate-feature is absent from skills/pyproject.toml testpaths while CI's test-infra-skills job runs a bare `uv run pytest` from skills/ — the new skill tests wp-wiring must add would never execute in CI.

Verified IndexScopes.allows in skills/validate-packages/scripts/context_impact.py lines 174-178: deny is evaluated before read_allow, confirming the same argument PLAN_ITERATE used to drop `deny: openspec/specs/**` applies unchanged to the surviving `deny: openspec/contracts/**`.

Ran the mechanical gates: `openspec validate trace-requirements-to-contracts --strict` valid; validate_work_packages.py VALID on schema/depends_on_refs/dag_cycles/lock_keys; all 14 ADDED requirements carry SHALL on their first line; the skill-workflow MODIFIED heading matches its archived base at openspec/specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:1548 exactly and drops no base clause; every task design-decision and scenario reference resolves.

decisions.decision: Outcome is not_converged despite consensus-plan.json reporting blocking_count=0.
decisions.rationale: consensus_synthesizer.py computes blocking as (status == confirmed AND disposition == fix), and marks confirmed only when finding descriptions match above a lexical similarity threshold. Four reviewers described the same defects in materially different words, so every finding landed 'unconfirmed' and blocking collapsed to zero. Deferring to that number would let a string-matching artifact certify a plan that four independent reviewers agree is not ready — the exact unfalsifiable-green failure this change exists to eliminate, reproduced in the apparatus reviewing it. Cross-confirmation was therefore done manually and is recorded in blocking_findings.

decisions.decision: D13's core mechanism is ACCEPTED; the blocking findings against it are all at its edges.
decisions.rationale: It was the designated review target and it held up. antigravity: 'architecturally sound, resolves staging deadlocks'. grok: verified by grep that no residual single-switch rule survives plan-findings F1, and judged the D12 distinction real rather than a rationalization — D12 forbade a second switch for the SAME claim's blocking bit, D13 switches a different claim with a different owner. codex did not challenge the split itself. No reviewer could construct an opted-in-but-not-blocking state under D13. The one state D13 makes inexpressible — recording a requirement exclusion without turning reverse enforcement on — is real, was found by two reviewers, and is an intentional adoption cliff rather than a defect. What must be fixed is the four unspecified edges, not the decision.

decisions.decision: The gatekeeper's wp-model write_allow widening must NOT be applied; PLAN_ITERATE's refutation is upheld unanimously.
decisions.rationale: Judged on the merits as instructed, by four reviewers independently reading the real models and generators rather than the plan's prose. All four reached the same conclusion with the same evidence: the four archetype-only models are not reachable from InterfaceDescriptor (confirmed against the generated $defs, not merely against the class hierarchy), and exclude_defaults=True on the flag/positional/command dumps keeps evaluation/descriptor.yaml byte-identical while the field's default is absent. Widening would have licensed exactly the drift those two --check gates exist to catch. The load-bearing artifact is task 2.2's model-placement constraint; keep it prominent, because a reviewer who does not read it will re-raise the gatekeeper's suggestion.

decisions.decision: Filed the contracts-inventory drift as a critical finding even though it resembles the refuted gatekeeper suggestion.
decisions.rationale: It is a different file, a different producer and a different gate. The gatekeeper's claim was about pydantic-generated artifacts under packages/gen-eval/ and is wrong. This one is about docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md, generated by the api.contracts producer from a raw rglob over openspec/contracts/**/*.schema.json, and enforced by the context-drift-gate CI job. Task 2.0 promotes two schemas into that tree, so the inventory's count and rows change and the gate reds, with the file outside every package's write_allow. Verified by reading the producer and confirming the gate is currently green on this tree.

decisions.decision: Did not re-dispatch pi after its failure.
decisions.rationale: pi returned in 1.6 seconds with 'Invalid JSON output' — the known failure signature, and far too fast to have read any artifact. Quorum was met at 3 vendors plus the primary, and the review_dispatcher discards stdout on parse failure so there is nothing to recover. Re-dispatching stricter is the documented remedy but would not change the outcome, which is already not_converged on 11 blocking findings.

next_steps: PLAN_ITERATE iteration 1 must fix the 11 blocking findings listed in blocking_findings below. Seven are spec/design text, four are work-packages.yaml scope or dependency changes; none requires rethinking D13's core split.

Fix the four D13 edges together, they are one coherent edit: (a) malformed/unreadable/schema-invalid traceability-exclusions.yaml must fail the gate naming the file and must never read as not-opted-in; (b) decide and specify whether a cross-capability exclusion may suppress the foreign capability's reverse completeness — recommended answer is no, restrict the file to its own capability; (c) resolve the direct contradiction between 'a capability with a spec and no contracts is untraced, run SHALL NOT fail' and 'reverse SHALL be enforced exactly when the file exists'; (d) make the opt-in TRANSITION visible to change scope.

(d) is the sharpest finding of the review and no prior phase saw it: flipping a switch widens enforcement over surfaces the diff never touched, so change scope cannot check the change that flips it. Adding the first traceability block to one operation opts the whole document in (D6) but only the edited node is touched; creating the exclusions file opts the whole capability in (D13) but only requirements named by new exclusions are touched. Fix: when a document first becomes traced, treat all of its operations as touched; when a capability first becomes reverse-enforced, treat its whole effective requirement set as touched. Without this, task 4.2b greens at validate-feature and reds main.

Fix the CI-context error in D12 and task 5.7 that compounds (d): a push-triggered job on main runs AFTER the merge, so it cannot block anything. D12's table and 5.7's note both reason 'not scheduled, because a scheduled run cannot block a merge' and then choose a trigger with the same defect. Make the sweep a required pull_request/merge_group check (optionally also on push to main as a post-merge sweep), and reword the requirement so 'blocks' maps to a genuinely pre-merge context.

Define 'contract document' normatively — it is used 20+ times, is what forward opt-in and the fail-closed rule are keyed on, and is nowhere defined. The real tree makes it urgent: openspec/contracts/ holds 13 .schema.json files, gen-eval-framework/cli/gen-eval.yaml, code-search/v2.yaml (a full OpenAPI 3.1 document at the capability root, outside the README's own layout), and after 4.2b the exclusions file itself, which a naive **/*.yaml glob would parse as a contract.

Resolve the capability-naming divergence before task 5.7 lands, or the sweep reds main on merge on three capabilities the change never touches: phase-record, project-context-refresh and prototyping have contract directories and no openspec/specs/<name>/spec.md, and the fail-closed requirement has no opt-in escape for that state.

Add an explicit GREEN counterpart to task 4.3's RED demonstrations: a task or final-checkpoint item recording `check_traceability.py --scope capability` exiting zero across every capability on the merge candidate. 4.3 proves the gate can fail; nothing currently proves the unmutated tree passes. Re-size task 4.2b against its real denominator — 20 archived gen-eval-framework requirements + this change's own 14 + roughly 17 from task 4.1 is about 51 decisions inside one [M] task.

Work-packages scope fixes: add docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md to wp-model (plus a `make context-refresh` step in task 2.0 and a context-drift-gate verification step); add skills/pyproject.toml to wp-wiring and register tests/validate-feature in testpaths; add openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/templates/change-context.md to wp-matrix; drop the inert `deny: openspec/contracts/**` from wp-gate, wp-matrix and wp-wiring.

Make wp-wiring's DISPATCH PRECONDITION machine-readable — flagged by all four reviewers. depends_on lists only [wp-gate, wp-matrix] while the prose requires human tasks 4.1/4.2/4.2b (and 5.2 for the sweep demo) to have landed. tasks.md's own edges are also short: 5.6 depends on 4.2 but not 4.2b, 5.7 on 5.2 but not 4.2b. Either add a blocked_on_tasks-style field the scheduler honours, or split wp-wiring into a forward-wiring package and a sweep-demonstration package gated on a recorded human checkpoint.

Two smaller text fixes with no scope impact: the operation-side `excluded` object in traceability.schema.json carries only `reason` and cannot name an operation, so the scenario 'an exclusion naming an operation that no longer exists SHALL fail' is unimplementable as written — the stale check is meaningful only for requirement-side entries; and contracts/README.md still says splitting the coordinator surface 'costs nothing in rigour', which D10 explicitly corrected to forward rigour only, a pre-D13 leftover that will re-teach the wrong staging model to whoever implements task 5.2.

Do NOT re-open the wp-model write_allow question. It has now been examined by four independent reviewers against the source and settled; re-raising it costs an iteration and licenses real schema drift.

On the next PLAN_REVIEW, reset findings_trend rather than comparing counts against this run: iteration 1 will rewrite the D13 edges and the touched-set definition, so a lower count would measure the rewrite, not convergence.
blocking_findings: B1 (4 reviewers: claude#3, antigravity#3, codex#4, grok#2) — the reverse opt-in switch has no fail-closed rule. An unparseable, schema-invalid, empty or unreadable traceability-exclusions.yaml reads as 'not opted in', silently disabling the direction D3 says nothing else detects. Inverts check_coverage_completeness.py lines 163-176, the precedent D4 claims to lift wholesale, which fails on both a missing and a malformed exclusions file.

B2 (3 reviewers: claude#4, codex#1, grok#4) — cross-capability requirement exclusions are permitted by traceability-exclusions.schema.json's field description and specified nowhere. Either capability A can launder capability B's reverse gaps without B's owner, or the schema description is false.

B3 (4 reviewers: claude#(next_steps), antigravity#4, codex#3, grok#5) — wp-wiring's DISPATCH PRECONDITION is prose-only; depends_on = [wp-gate, wp-matrix] lets a scheduler dispatch it before the human artifacts exist, so the 5.6/5.7 RED demonstrations can only run against fixtures — the mirror-verification failure this change exists to end.

B4 (grok#1, sole reviewer, unrefuted) — the opt-in TRANSITION is invisible to change scope. Flipping either switch widens enforcement over untouched surfaces, so validate-feature greens on the very change that flips it and main reds afterwards.

B5 (codex#2, sole reviewer, unrefuted) — a push-triggered job on main runs after the merge, so the 'blocking' full sweep in D12 and task 5.7 cannot block a merge; the plan rejects cron for exactly this reason and then picks a trigger with the same defect.

B6 (claude#1, empirically verified) — phase-record, project-context-refresh and prototyping have contract directories under openspec/contracts/ and no openspec/specs/<name>/spec.md; the fail-closed requirement has no opt-in escape, so the blocking sweep reds main on merge on three untouched capabilities.

B7 (claude#2, empirically verified) — 'contract document' is used 20+ times, is what forward opt-in and the fail-closed rule key on, and is never defined; the real tree contains four different artifact kinds under openspec/contracts/ that a discovery rule must distinguish.

B8 (claude#6, empirically verified) — task 2.0's schema promotion drifts docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md (rendered by the api.contracts producer from an rglob over openspec/contracts/**/*.schema.json, carrying a count and per-schema rows) and reds the context-drift-gate CI job; the file is in no package's write_allow. Distinct from the refuted gatekeeper claim.

B9 (claude#5, empirically verified) — skills/tests/validate-feature is not in skills/pyproject.toml testpaths, so the skill tests the skill-workflow ADDED requirement demands are never run by CI's bare `uv run pytest` in skills/; skills/pyproject.toml is in no package's write_allow.

B10 (claude#7, corroborated in scale by grok#11) — nothing requires the unmutated tree to pass at capability scope before merge. Task 4.3 proves RED on two mutations; the GREEN counterpart is absent, while task 4.2b must triage roughly 51 requirements inside one [M] task.

NON-BLOCKING but fix in the same pass (claude#8, severity nit) — the skill-workflow ADDED requirement wires the gate into /validate-feature unconditionally, but that SKILL.md ships via install.sh into consumer repositories with no packages/gen-eval/ and no openspec/contracts/; the skill's own gen-eval phase already solves this with detection plus an explicit printed SKIP.
